text: {"answerable": true, "answer": "Ordinary convolutional layers assume the data lie on a regular grid, as image pixels do, but atoms in molecules are not on a grid and can be located at arbitrary positions, so a conventional filter tensor is not applicable [W2778051509#006][W2726670313#006]. Unevenly spaced inputs like atom positions cannot be handled by a grid filter, and re-sampling onto a grid requires an interpolation scheme that is itself a challenge and may need many grid points [W2726670313#006]. The atoms' precise locations carry essential physical information that would be lost if discretized [W2726670313#001]. SchNet therefore uses continuous filters generated by a filter-generating network that maps atom positions to filter values [W2778051509#006][W2726670313#006]. A discrete filter also cannot capture subtle positional changes, leading to discontinuous energy predictions [W2726670313#005]."}
